rationale: Candidate A correctly identifies the defect (ThreadLocal leak in a pooled thread environment), explains the growth over time (thread reuse + lack of removal), and provides the correct fix (calling remove() in a finally block). Candidate B provides an incorrect fix; using a WeakHashMap does not prevent the map itself from growing indefinitely if entries are added to it across requests on the same thread, and it fails to address the core requirement of using remove() to bound the lifetime to the request.
